fields.why: Acute rates are ranked across 6 age groups (Figure 1, Results), and newly reported chronic cases carry rates for 7 age groups and the birth cohorts in the Table, so an outcome is measured per SPD group.
Sex is a pair (male vs female); birth cohort stands for age, and no other SPD is reported (the SES strata were suppressed).

The only test is a blanket 'p-values for all chi-squared tests were <0.001' with no stated contrast, placed in the chronic-case paragraph; reading it as an omnibus test across the 7 chronic age groups (rule F2) is defensible, but so is side by side for both entries, since no claim cites the test. Acute rates by age as side by side is right; the flag on that entry is a weak alarm.

brief_issues: The brief does not say how to read a blanket chi-square note ('p-values for all chi-squared tests were <0.001') whose contrasts are not identified: whether it makes the SPD tables omnibus tests (rule F2) or leaves them side by side because no claim rests on it.
